synth.baseline:
TODAY (draft L), measured along a realistic walking path that goes around the end of the island. Every concept below is measured the same way.

WALK: From the island center (58.5,48), cut diagonally through the island/range aisle to the hall mouth (66,37), which is about 14 ft. Then go about 22.5 ft east down the hall to x 88.5, and 4 ft through the small vestibule to the bedroom door (x 87-90 on y 32). That is about 40 ft in total. If you walk it on a strict right-angle path, it is 46 ft. From the garage entry door (87-90, y 40) it is 8 ft straight across the hall, and the garage door looks directly at the bedroom door.

CORRIDOR: The hall runs from x 68 to x 86 (4 ft wide, 18 ft long). It has the office sound wall on one side and the stair, garage and drop-zone walls on the other. About 14.5 ft of it is walled on both sides, with no daylight and nothing to do in it but walk. Only about 7 ft (x 71.5-78.5) is a true narrow tube; past x 78.5 it widens at the drop zone.

VIEW: None toward the pond. The bedroom (86-106 x 16-32) has one window wall, the 8 ft slider at x 106, and it looks at the east side porch. From the bed (98,22), the nearest water is about 36-40 ft away and the falls (37.5,-41) about 87 ft away. Both are blocked by the dressing room and the bath. The only room in the suite that sees the pond is the bath, through its tub window.

PRIVACY: Good. The office and the bath stand between the bedroom and the party terrace. The weak spot is the garage door, 8 ft from the bedroom door.

WHY IT FEELS LIKE A HALLWAY: 40 ft is not a long walk. It feels like one because half of it runs down a narrow, dark service hall that the suite shares with the garage, laundry, stair, powder room and office. Putting the bedroom at the back in the usual way (bath and closet in front, bedroom behind them) would add another 20-28 ft of passage. That is the long hallway Melissa is describing, and it is why the earlier study ruled out the 'flip'. There are two ways around it. Either the bedroom moves into a room that already touches the kitchen end of the hall (the office slot), or the extra distance is spent inside a real furnished room (an entry lounge or morning room) instead of a hall.

concepts.title: Suite takes the office slot; bedroom faces the pond, 27 ft from the island
concepts.strategy: Swap two rooms inside the walls we already have. The office's spot (68-86) already sits on the house's back line, starts right where the great room ends, and looks at the pond. The primary bedroom moves there behind a small foyer, and the office moves into today's primary bedroom. Melissa's bath and dressing room stay where they are and are now entered from the side of the bedroom.
concepts.proposal:
The footprint and roof stay the same. All changes are inside today's walls.
- FOYER 68-78 x 27-34 (10'x7'). You enter through today's office door (x 68.5-71.5 on the hall), right where the hall leaves the kitchen. It has a morning bar (coffee, fridge drawers) on the x 78 wall and a small bench. A 3 ft pocket door at x 70-73 on y 27 leads into the bedroom.
- PRIMARY BEDROOM 68-86 x 5-27 (18'x22', 396 sf). The back wall (y 5, x 69-85) becomes a 16 ft multi-slide glass wall onto a private garden. A small corner glass at x 68 (y 5.5-8, kept below the outdoor-kitchen eave) lines up with the falls. The king bed's head is on the foyer wall, so the bed faces the pond. The sitting area is at the glass. The x 68 wall stays a double-stud sound wall.
- DRESSING ROOM 86-106 x 8-16 and BATH 86-106 x -2.5..8 stay as drawn. They get a new 3 ft opening from the bedroom (x 86, y 10.5-13.5) and a pocket door from the bedroom straight into the bath (x 86, y 5.3-7.8). The old opening from the bedroom to the dressing room at x 87-90 on y 16 is walled in, and the mirror stays on the x 86 end.

- PRIVATE GARDEN 64-86 x -6..5. It has a screen at x 64, 6 ft high from y 3 to 10 and dropping to 42 in from y -6 to 3 so the falls line stays open. There is NO wall on the pond side, only planting 18 in or lower, so the water stays visible from the bed.

The falls are about 76 ft away, seen through the small corner glass at x 68 (the line crosses at y 7.2). From the sitting area (73,8.5), water is about 15 ft and the falls about 61 ft, straight out through the back glass. Today the bedroom has no pond view at all.

The party terrace stops at about x 64, and its last 5 ft beside the outdoor kitchen is taken into the garden behind a 6 ft screen. Use motorized sheers on the corner glass. The outdoor-kitchen U currently sits on this wall, so the grill must move to the x 46 end (or this leg becomes a cold bar). Guests pass a solid suite door into a foyer, never the bedroom. The garage, stair, under-stair closet, server room and bedroom wing do not change.
concepts.tradeoffs: For: it fixes both of Melissa's points for the least money. The walk is about 27 ft from the island (19 ft to the suite's own door), against 40 today, with essentially no corridor. The bedroom is truly on the pond, there is no roof or footprint change, and Melissa's bath stays as drawn. Against: Michael's office gets about 30% smaller and trades its pond view for the side porch. The dressing room is still the 20'x8' strip until option B is added. The bedroom shares walls with the dining room, the outdoor kitchen and the powder room, so it needs good sound walls. The garage walk grows from 8 ft to about 31 ft.

The layout is kept but in a smaller room, and the office entry is no longer across from the stairs. The powder room moves (option A finishes kept). The outdoor-kitchen U moves. synth.why:
OFFICE-SWAP is the only idea that gives Michael and Melissa both things at once, and it is also the cheapest. The bedroom ends up truly on the pond: a 16 ft glass wall, the sitting area about 15 ft from the water, and the falls visible through the corner glass. The walk gets SHORTER, from about 40 ft today to about 27 ft from the island, with essentially no corridor (2 ft against 14.5 ft today). There is no roof or footprint change, and Melissa's bath stays as drawn. The price is Michael's office. It moves into today's primary bedroom with the same couch, desk and TV arrangement, but it is about 30% smaller and looks at the side porch instead of the pond. The grill also has to come off the old office wall. That is a real decision only Michael can make.

If he says no to moving the office, BEDROOM-FIRST is the answer. It touches no firm decision and keeps today's walk length to the suite door. The bedroom becomes the first room you enter, with the bed facing a glass bay on the pond and the closet and bath to the side, so no new passage is added. But the existing 14.5 ft service hall stays. POND-PAVILION is the upgrade path from OFFICE-SWAP if they want more glass and closet. FALLS-VIEW is the only plan that shows the falls from the pillow, but its 56 ft walk works against Melissa's request.

Compared with the earlier recommendation (study option B, bath pushed back and bedroom left at the front of the wing): option B fixed the bath but left the bedroom with no pond view and kept the walk down the service hall. The earlier objections to a 'flipped' bedroom were a smaller bath, sitting 2 ft from the party terrace, and hitting the berm. OFFICE-SWAP avoids all three: the bath is unchanged, the bedroom faces a walled private garden 11 ft or more from water, and nothing comes near the berm. Option B can still be added on top later for a bigger bath and closet.

Ideas considered and dropped:
- Swapping wings (primary into the bedroom wing). It removes the hall, but it lengthens the walk to 54 ft and the garage walk to 84 ft, and it puts the bedroom beside the party porch with the swim beach and fire pit in front of the bed.
- Flipping the stack in place behind a dressing-room vestibule. The roof failed the drainage check, and the walk reads as hall plus closet passage.
- A pavilion beyond a dressing gallery. The walk grows to 63 ft.

decisions.q: Michael, will you move your office into today's primary bedroom (20x16, same couch/desk/TV layout, side porch instead of pond windows) so the primary can take the office's pond-facing spot?
decisions.rec: Yes. It is the only way to make the walk shorter and give the bedroom the pond. If not, go with BEDROOM-FIRST.

decisions.q: Can the outdoor-kitchen grill move to the x 46 end of the U (or the x 68 leg become a cold bar)?
decisions.rec: Yes, move the grill to the x 46 end. Keep the x 68 wall a double-stud sound wall.

decisions.q: Should the new pond shape put the swim basin west of about x 60 and a quiet lily/wetland cove behind the primary suite (shore at y -8 or further back)?
decisions.rec: Yes. Swimmers 11 ft from the bed is the privacy problem; quiet water there is the view.

decisions.q: Is it OK if the falls are seen from the bedroom's sitting chairs rather than from the pillow?
decisions.rec: Yes. Only FALLS-VIEW gets the falls from bed, and it costs a 56 ft walk and the most terrace.

decisions.q: Melissa, is today's 20x8 dressing room enough, or should we also push the bath back (option B) for a bigger closet and bath?
decisions.rec: Start without it. Add option B (or the 270 sf closet + 200 sf bath version) if she wants more closet; it fits on top of OFFICE-SWAP.

decisions.q: Do you want the glass-pavilion upgrade (bedroom pushed 7.5 ft into the yard, entered through the closet)?
decisions.rec: Not now. It costs more and depends on the pond redesign; keep it as the upgrade path.

decisions.q: Still no island in the closet?
decisions.rec: Keep a bench or ottoman, as Melissa asked.
